name: Interpret what a retrieval question needs
summary: An isolated host LLM interprets a question into typed information needs; production retrieval does not call it.

steps.label: Prepare the question and offered meanings
steps.description: The system validates the question, context and catalog of offered meanings within the size limit, adding as candidates only identifiers given or named in the question.
produces: task_input/input_payload: null|object (optional; default null; applies retrieval_needs_request schema)

document_types.execution_report: Actual test execution or publication receipt; not declarations
document_types.schema: Machine-readable schema or versioned contract definition

relationships.all_descendants: Every descendant under the target, including intermediate levels, subject to later explicit completeness checks; execution depth caps do not redefine this need
relationships.children_direct: Direct children only, one hierarchy hop
relationships.incoming_dependencies_direct: Requirements that directly depend on the target, incoming dependency edges, one hop
relationships.linked_tests: Declared tests linked to the target; no execution proof implied
relationships.parent_direct: Immediate parent only, one hierarchy hop

required_fields.compatibility: Contract compatibility obligations and version constraints
required_fields.content: Relevant source code or document content
required_fields.covered_by: Declared test links, not proof tests executed
required_fields.criteria: Acceptance criteria, exact required behavior or canonical clauses
required_fields.level: Requirement hierarchy level, e.g. L2 or L3
required_fields.mapping: Inspected field transformations or producer/consumer handoffs
required_fields.provenance: Canonical identity, source revision, path and field/line locators
required_fields.status: Requirement lifecycle status such as active or deprecated; never implementation progress
required_fields.test_spec: Test requirements and must-catch wrong implementations
required_fields.work_status: Implementation progress such as todo, in progress, done; distinct from lifecycle

steps.label: Interpret all information needs together
steps.description: The host model reads the request and, using only the offered labels, interprets in one pass which entity types, targets, fields, documents and relationships the question needs.

examples.label: Candidate output projection — actual N03; echoed question/scope and other fields omitted.

steps.label: Submit the interpretation to its wait
steps.description: The host controller wraps the interpretation for the original run and wait and submits it to the kernel, leaving unknown model or token usage unclaimed.

examples.label: Submission wrapper projection — actual N03; response body omitted.

steps.label: Check the response before accepting it
steps.description: The kernel checks that the response fits the current wait and schema, keeps the question unchanged and uses only offered, non-overlapping labels, which proves form, not correctness.

examples.label: Response projection — actual N03, not a complete output.

steps.label: Record acceptance and resume the run
steps.description: The kernel records the accepted response in its durable ledger before resuming the run, so an identical replay changes nothing and a conflicting one is refused.

examples.label: Accepted-ledger projection — actual N03; submission body omitted.

steps.label: Normalize the interpretation
steps.description: The kernel adds structural gaps to the unresolved reasons, marks the interpretation as decided or needing resolution, and records a model only if the host reported one.

examples.label: Normalized output projection — actual N03; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields are in the linked contract.

steps.label: Return the typed needs
steps.description: The kernel returns the typed needs as a completed interpretation, which does not mean any retrieval or answer has happened.

value.rationale: The population is every descendant of the named root whose level is L2 or L3, including intermediate descendants that are themselves parents. Exclude only TQ-500f and group the complete count by implementation work_status. Direct children and lifecycle status would not preserve the request.

branches.label: Reject an invalid request
branches.condition: Input is malformed, ungrounded or outside the request bounds
branches.description: The system rejects the task before any host wait is created, without trimming the catalog, inventing targets or reinterpreting the question.

io_contracts.not_applicable: The Python build_llm_needs_task call raises a validation/value error before a TaskInput or RunEnvelope exists. The rejected arguments do not become an accepted request DTO. There is no separate serialized error payload at this API boundary; the callable does not start a host wait.

branches.label: Keep waiting across a restart
branches.condition: The host has not submitted a response
branches.description: The kernel keeps the saved wait open, even across a restart, so the original run resumes when a valid response finally arrives.

branches.label: Refuse the wrong submission
branches.condition: The wrapper, actor, run, wait, revision or response kind is invalid
branches.description: The kernel refuses the submission without recording it or changing the run, so the host must resend it correctly for the current wait.

examples.label: Illustrative stale-revision submission, rejected against revision 1

branches.label: Return to the host for correction
branches.condition: The payload fails schema or request-bound validation and its first correction remains
branches.description: The kernel records the rejection and sends the request back to the host with the reasons, allowing one corrected response.

examples.label: Illustrative first rejected payload; same interaction is reissued

rejections.message: the response does not match its schema

branches.label: Stop after correction fails
branches.condition: A second payload fails schema or request-bound validation after the one allowed correction
branches.description: The kernel records the second rejection, fails the work item and closes the wait without accepting any response.

examples.label: Illustrative failure after the initial invalid payload and one invalid correction

error.message: host output stayed invalid after 2 submissions (last: schema_invalid)

branches.label: Return unsupported or unresolved needs
branches.condition: Valid output contains unresolved reasons or structural missing dimensions
branches.description: The kernel keeps the question, the selected and uncertain values and the reasons, and returns the interpretation as needing resolution without asking anyone or searching.

examples.label: Illustrative exhaustive-count interpretation with unresolved hierarchy

branches.label: Report a conversion failure
branches.condition: Accepted submission cannot produce a valid normalized result
branches.description: The kernel reports a failed result instead of a completed interpretation, even though the response was already accepted.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A question names TQ-500f and supplies a catalog with no target IDs
acceptance_scenarios.when: The task builder validates and prepares the request
acceptance_scenarios.then: TQ-500f is added as a literal candidate without selecting it; invalid or oversized input is refused before start.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A validated task and the isolated experiment service
acceptance_scenarios.then: Fixed routing selects only host.retrieval_needs; no Jev call, repository retrieval or production activation occurs.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The isolated run requests host interpretation
acceptance_scenarios.then: The actual input artifact and typed packet are persisted and the run checkpoints waiting_host.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The saved packet and operational input
acceptance_scenarios.when: The external host interprets the question
acceptance_scenarios.then: A candidate supplies all five selected/uncertain dimensions and all modes without retrieving or answering the question.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A candidate output and its pending host packet
acceptance_scenarios.when: The host controller submits the result
acceptance_scenarios.then: The submission names the original run, interaction, expected revision and output schema with a valid host actor.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An otherwise valid response selects an unoffered ID or changes source_scope
acceptance_scenarios.when: Submission validation checks the actual pending request
acceptance_scenarios.then: The payload is rejected before accepted-ledger persistence; schema validity alone is insufficient for acceptance.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A submission passes schema and request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The durable accepted entry is written before the original LangGraph wait resumes; identical replays do not apply a second interpretation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Accepted output has no structural gaps, no explicit unresolved reasons and no reported host usage
acceptance_scenarios.when: The host operation normalizes the result
acceptance_scenarios.then: The typed output is decided with model_id=null while retaining any uncertain alternatives; this is not a semantic-correctness guarantee.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An offered target ID is neither literal in the question nor supplied in known_ids
acceptance_scenarios.when: The task builder validates the request
acceptance_scenarios.then: The request is refused before host work is opened.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The run is waiting_host and the process restarts
acceptance_scenarios.then: The same persisted wait remains available for its matching response; no new model result is assumed.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A response wrapper carries an invalid actor ID or stale revision
acceptance_scenarios.then: It is refused without accepted-ledger or graph mutation; it is not reported as needs_resolution.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The first pending host payload fails schema or request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The same interaction allows one correction and returns to host interpretation and resubmission without an accepted ledger entry.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An accepted payload retains an unsupported meaning in unresolved
acceptance_scenarios.when: The operation derives its normalized status
acceptance_scenarios.then: The interpretation completes with needs_resolution and its reasons; it neither answers the question nor opens a human wait.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An accepted submission reports a host model ID longer than the output contract allows
acceptance_scenarios.then: It returns a failed capability result without crashing or claiming a completed interpretation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A normalized typed output with decided or needs_resolution
acceptance_scenarios.then: The interpretation completes and returns typed needs with an interpretation-only limitation; no retrieval or final answer is produced.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The first invalid payload was rejected and the one allowed correction was requested
acceptance_scenarios.when: A second payload fails schema or request-bound checks
acceptance_scenarios.then: The work item fails and the wait is removed without an accepted submission or completed interpretation result.

provenance.note:
Search and scope
Searched artifacts[], by_component and by_flow: the existing retrieval journey and its query, search, traversal, build and baseline artifacts do not describe this callable interpreter. Extend [the existing draft](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieve-project-knowledge.flow.json#interpret-needs) with an explicitly proposed/unwired call-site; keep implementation detail in this bounded child. The current baseline only links it as separate experiment evidence. No new screens, entities, AC links or approvals are invented. Built means the isolated experiment exists in this worktree; readiness remains draft. The displayed normalize/return phases describe existing conversion code, not new runtime steps. The Atlas schema records branch origins only; return routes are explicit in branch text and links.

Input contract
leafcutter.retrieval_needs_request.v1: original_question; optional context, known_ids and source_scope; catalog with exactly entity_types, target_ids, required_fields, document_types and relationships. Each dimension maps offered labels to meanings, at most 64 labels. Scope and caller Actor are separate TaskInput parameters; permissions are empty. Catalog meanings describe possible information needs, not evidence that a backend can retrieve them.

The builder preserves literal/supplied target candidates. Context and known IDs are unverified hints. Echoing source_scope does not verify its repository, paths or revision. [Typed contracts](kernel/contracts/retrieval_needs.py) · [Frozen example input](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/inputs/N03.input.json).

Output contract and example
leafcutter.retrieval_needs_output.v1 returns the unchanged question/scope, selections and uncertain arrays for all five dimensions, detail_mode, completeness, hierarchy_scope, scope_resolution, unresolved, rationale, engine=host_llm, normalized status and model_id.

Saved N03 input: Count all L2 and L3 descendants of TQ-500f, excluding only TQ-500f, grouped by work_status.
Saved output: entity_types=[ac]; target_ids=[TQ-500f]; required_fields=[level, work_status]; document_types=[ac_yaml]; relationships=[all_descendants]. detail_mode=fields; completeness=exhaustive_count; hierarchy_scope=exclude_root; scope_resolution=sufficient. All uncertain arrays and unresolved are empty; status=decided; model_id=null. This identifies what a later retrieval would need; it returns no count. [Original response](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/responses/N03.json).

Mode meanings
Detail: fields = requested facts; full_document = the whole selected item; bounded_context = the selected item plus requested surroundings; unknown retains a gap. Completeness: single_entity, selected_entities, exhaustive_set, exhaustive_count, examples or unknown. Hierarchy: not_applicable, exclude_root, exclude_parents, include_root or unknown. Scope resolution: sufficient, discovery_needed, user_choice_missing or unknown.

Normalization adds missing entity/document types, unknown detail/completeness, missing fields for fields mode, missing target IDs for identified targets, unresolved user choice/unknown scope, unknown hierarchy for exhaustive sets/counts, and selected_entities with only one target and no relationship. Nonempty uncertain arrays alone do not force needs_resolution. These are structural rules, not an oracle for semantic correctness.

Frozen evidence, not a runtime grading step
The [accepted trial](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/README.md) and [per-case results](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/results.md) record 12 durable accepted submissions and 12 completed interpretations, but only 8/12 frozen semantic passes. N01, N09 and N11 selected test_spec without required criteria for exact-AC obligations. N10 honestly retained unsupported payroll needs but used a prefixed explanation instead of the frozen exact needs_outside_catalog marker. It passed kernel acceptance and failed that semantic encoding check.

The separate prospective overlay passed 7/7 applicable host cases; it does not repair the four shared failures. Original Jev score remains 7/12. Reported deterministic coverage is 76 tests plus 82 subtests, including 18 new controlled cases. No tests or model trial are rerun by this flow; these are dated annotations. [Independent review](docs/analysis/retrieval-needs-llm-probe-2026-10-03/independent-review.md).

Boundaries and provenance
The external host chooses/configures its model; no Haiku or provider client is hardcoded here. The blind trial used a Codex host agent. Its exact model, underlying request count and tokens were unknown. One issued host operation is not one model HTTP call or an accepted response; ledger evidence establishes acceptance.

This flow does not select or run search methods, construct query arguments, retrieve source data, answer the question, call Jev, approve or train classifiers, self-learn, or activate fallback policy. Acceptance and decided are not guarantees of semantic correctness. [Architecture contract](docs/analysis/retrieval-needs-llm-probe-2026-10-03/contract-and-architecture.md).

Concrete contract review
Replaced descriptive handoff terms with actual model/artifact field paths, types, requiredness and defaults. Added step-local JSON examples following accepted N03. Complete request/output payloads are copied from saved evidence and validated against canonical JSON Schemas plus typed models. Transport/ledger examples are explicitly projections; the TaskInput example is clearly reconstructed from the request and controller source, not a saved receipt. No new wire fields, runtime phases, mock entities, statuses or integration are introduced. Model prefixes in field labels identify ownership and are not serialized wrapper keys.

Reassessed the isolated interpreter against the current source. Replaced generic branch exemptions with actual wait, submission, rejection-list, unresolved-output and failure-result contracts. Examples explicitly distinguish observed N03 receipts from counterfactual branch illustrations. Runtime, frozen evaluation and approval statuses are unchanged.
Removed obsolete display instructions from the authored narrative for the structured Atlas contract view. Preserved exact handoff metadata, examples, experimental scope and runtime limits.

Reconciled current TaskInput admission bounds and entity-context host-artifact channels after merging main. Historical N03 receipts remain unchanged and explicitly historical; experiment-only scope, typed request/output, topology, AC status and semantic evaluation limits are preserved.
